title: 2008 AMC 8 Problem 12
statement: A ball is dropped from a height of \(3\) meters. On its first bounce it rises to a height of \(2\) meters. It keeps falling and bouncing to \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the height it reached in the previous bounce. On which bounce will it not rise to a height of \(0.5\) meters?

solutions.text:
The first bounce rises to \(2\) meters. Each later bounce is \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) of the previous bounce.

The fourth bounce rises to \(2\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^3=\dfrac{16}{27}\), which is greater than \(\dfrac{1}{2}\).

The fifth bounce rises to \(2\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^4=\dfrac{32}{81}\), which is less than \(\dfrac{1}{2}\).

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: List the bounce heights by multiplying by \(\frac{2}{3}\) each time.
Compare the fourth and fifth bounce heights with \(\frac{1}{2}\).
